title: D. B. Cooper
subtitle: Northwest Orient Flight 305 · 1971
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, the rain-soaked Pacific Northwest of November 1971 at dusk and night, wet airport tarmac, dark fir forest and grey river, cold blue-grey light, melancholy and uncanny, period 1971 detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Portland, Oregon. November twenty-fourth, nineteen seventy-one. A man who called himself Dan Cooper boarded a flight to Seattle.
beats.img: A rain-wet airport apron at dusk with a 1970s three-engine passenger jet parked beside a portable boarding stair, sodium lamps reflecting on wet tarmac, low grey Pacific Northwest overcast, no people.

beats.vo: In the air, he passed a note. He said he had a bomb. He asked for two hundred thousand dollars, and four parachutes.
beats.img: Four packed parachute rigs lying side by side on a bare concrete floor under a single hanging work lamp in an empty 1970s airport hangar, rain-streaked windows, moody shadows, no people.

beats.vo: In Seattle, the passengers were released, and the money was delivered. The plane took off again, into the night.
beats.img: A 1970s passenger jet climbing away from a rainy runway at night, its lights blurred by drizzle, dark wet tarmac and runway lights in the foreground, cold and quiet, no people.

beats.vo: Somewhere over southwest Washington, the rear stairs came down. When the plane landed in Reno, he was gone.
beats.img: Looking down from high altitude at night onto a dark rain-soaked forested wilderness, black ridges of fir trees under heavy cloud, a faint river glint far below, no people.

beats.vo: In nineteen eighty, a boy found some of the money on a bank of the Columbia River. The man has never been identified.
beats.img: A grey sandy riverbank on a wide calm river under overcast sky, damp driftwood and a small hollow in the sand, misty forested shore beyond, quiet and unresolved, no people.

facts.claim: On November 24, 1971, a man who bought a ticket as 'Dan Cooper' boarded Northwest Orient Flight 305, a ~30-minute Portland, Oregon to Seattle flight
In flight he passed a note to a flight attendant saying he had a bomb; demanded $200,000 and four parachutes
In Seattle the passengers were released in exchange for the money and parachutes; the plane took off again at night
He opened the aft door, lowered the rear airstair and parachuted at night over southwest Washington
In February 1980 an eight-year-old boy found packets of the ransom money (serials matched) on the Columbia River bank at Tena Bar
The hijacker has never been identified; FBI suspended active investigation July 2016; no identification as of 2026 (Jan 2026 file release, Dec 2025 parachute return, no breakthrough)
